methodology: Status microbenchmark uses the unchanged pinned standalone VM sources compiled with Zig 0.16.0 -O3 -DNDEBUG; storage contains one initialized 80-byte metadata item.

Same historical Doom artifact used in previous status controls, plus a variant with only memory_bytes changed from 16 MiB to 10 MiB. All guest code, initial data and addresses are identical within this controlled pair.

Cached mode prepares once outside measured calls; fresh mode rebuilds and destroys preparation inside each timed sample. Both construct a fresh VM and execute method 4 each time. Neither restores or runs the Doom engine.
51 sequential samples per mode per artifact; summary medians omit sample 0. Raw rows retain it. Separate span medians need not add exactly.

The earlier approximately 11 ms gameplay timer includes VM construction and image copy. It excludes code preparation and prepared image creation. Thus the copy is not an additional full untimed cost on the cached path.
Standalone storage is a local map and does not model node DB RPC, scheduling, authentication or block production. These numbers do not fully explain node transaction latency.
The production default was rebuilt with a 10 MiB linker declaration. Its full allocated layout ends at 0x9ac018, below 10 MiB; all addresses and the 8 MiB heap capacity are retained.

The newly rebuilt artifact has a different code hash from the historical artifact. A same-build 16 MiB linker control was also built and verified to differ from the current 10 MiB artifact only in the header memory-size field. Historical and rebuilt artifact measurements must not be treated as identical builds.

Current 10 MiB build validated with 1050 standalone gameplay ticks and persistence/replay/rollback checks, plus 35 real-node HTTP ticks and stale/malformed-input checks. Live timings are descriptive, not an isolated same-run measurement of the memory change.

validation.standaloneChecks: persistence, deterministic replay, stale/reinitialize rejection, out-of-gas rollback/retry, frame chunks
